newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Spain's Telefonica spent $240mln on Argentine deal.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Telefonica spent $240mln on Argentine deal.

text.p: Argentina's Techint on Friday said the company received $240 million for selling a 8.3 percent stake in Telefonica de Argentina's holding company to Telefonica de Espana.

Techint Executive Vice President Eduardo Baglietto said the company decided to sell its stake in Cointel because its core ownership position had eroded after numerous stakeholding changes. He also said that Telefonica de Espana had made an attractive offer.

"Our intention is not to be financial partners. We have a commanding industrial attitude so, in the face of that imbalance and the interesting offer by Telefonica de Espana, we decided to sell," Baglietto said.
The deal, announced on Thursday, brings Telefonica de Espana's stake in Cointel to 45.8 percent.

Sources from Telefonica de Argentina told Reuters that Telefonica de Espana was planning an imminent deal to purchase from Bank of Tokyo Mitsubishi a further 4.2 percent of Cointel, taking its total holding to 50 percent.
The other 50 percent of Cointel is in the hands of Argentina's CEI Citicorp Holdings SA, which is about 40 percent indirectly owned by Citibank.
CEI had a 50.2026 percent in Cointel but sold 0.2026 percent to Telefonica de Espana on Thursday.
Telefonica de Espana already controlled the management of Telefonica de Argentina, which was created in 1990 after the privatization of the former state phone company Entel.
Telefonica is the biggest of the two telephone companies that were formerly part of Entel. The other is Telecom which has about 46 percent of the market.
